data.description: C11-192 refuted its original premise (no c11-owned Button in any metadata-stack event; the 10s title came from Sentry grouping every hang into one issue) and deliberately did no view-tree work. This ticket owns the question the classifier makes answerable: once main-thread-hang/generic-metadata exists as its own Sentry issue, does it have meaningful distinct-user volume? Also compute the per-user spread of the pre-#401 generic-metadata captures (the 50-event bucket): if they came from the six users other than the 816-event outlier, this class is more widespread than its 5.7% suggests (adversarial-gemini's point from the C11-192 trident review). If the trend is real, open a fix ticket with a Time Profiler acceptance; if it stays near zero distinct users, close with that evidence. Note post-#401 throttling may starve the trend (see C11-192 review S7): state the observation window and the minimum event count for a verdict.
data.title: Is generic-metadata instantiation a real user-facing hang class? Judge from the post-classifier trend

data.body:
## Spike result: half (a) answered, half (b) blocked on shipping the classifier

### Method

Paged the **full** event set of both pre-classifier aggregate issues via the Sentry API: C11-30 (`main thread hang 2127ms`, 2804 events) and C11-31 (`main thread hang 9110ms (persist)`, 1959 events). **n = 4763 events, 20 distinct users, 32 distinct device hashes**, window 2026-07-25T00:45Z .. 2026-08-10T04:10Z (16.1 days). This is the complete population of both issues, not a sample: cursor paging ran to exhaustion on both.

Each event carries `contexts.hang.stack`. v0.58.0 and v0.61.0 both send `stack.prefix(24)`, so the top 24 frames are verbatim and contiguous. `MainThreadHangSignature.cause` uses `causeWindow = 16` and `moduleWindow = 8`, both inside that window, so re-running the shipped rules over these captures gives the **exact** cause the classifier would have assigned, not an approximation. Rules, needles, ordering, the `runloop-idle` special case and the module sets were transcribed verbatim from `Sources/MainThreadHangMonitor.swift` into a throwaway Python port. `phase` was deliberately not reproduced (phaseRules scan the whole 96-frame capture; only 24 frames survive the wire).

79 of 4763 events (1.7%) arrived with `stack: "[Filtered]"` after Sentry data scrubbing and are unclassifiable. They are reported as their own bucket rather than silently dropped.

### Cause x user, all events

| cause | events | distinct users | user-days | share | top-user share | conc. index |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| swiftui-update | 2653 | 17 | 67 | 55.7% | 59.1% | 1.12 |
| runloop-idle | 679 | 17 | 66 | 14.3% | 22.4% | 0.43 |
| appkit | 446 | 16 | 63 | 9.4% | 30.7% | 0.58 |
| other | 384 | 16 | 54 | 8.1% | 56.0% | 1.06 |
| **generic-metadata** | **273** | **13** | **43** | **5.7%** | **64.1%** | **1.22** |
| xpc-sync-wait | 194 | 8 | 17 | 4.1% | 91.8% | 1.74 |
| (scrubbed by Sentry) | 79 | 5 | 16 | 1.7% | 75.9% | 1.44 |
| lock-wait | 55 | 9 | 22 | 1.2% | 36.4% | 0.69 |

The outlier user (U01) is **52.6% of the whole corpus** (2505/4763), so "top-user share" only means outlier-driven when it runs well above that. Concentration index = top-user share / 52.6%.

### Episode-level view (recapture=false, the shape #401 now sends)

| cause | episodes | users | episodes/week | non-outlier episodes |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| swiftui-update | 1554 | 17 | 674 | 775 across 16 users |
| runloop-idle | 408 | 17 | 177 | 330 across 16 users |
| appkit | 323 | 16 | 140 | 230 across 15 users |
| other | 230 | 15 | 100 | 113 across 14 users |
| **generic-metadata** | **151** | **11** | **65** | **67 across 10 users** |
| xpc-sync-wait | 57 | 8 | 25 | 12 across 7 users |
| lock-wait | 39 | 7 | 17 | 27 across 6 users |

### Verdict on (a): widespread, not outlier-driven

`generic-metadata` is **273 events from 13 of 20 distinct users** (65% of everyone who reported a hang at all), on **43 distinct user-days**, **151 distinct episodes across 11 users**. The outlier contributes 175 of 273 events; **12 other users contribute the remaining 98**, and **9 users have 2 or more** so this is not a one-off per person. Adversarial-gemini's hypothesis is confirmed in substance: the 5.7% volume share badly understates the reach. By distinct users it is the fifth-broadest class of eight and sits within one user of `other` (16) and three of `appkit` (16); only the three big buckets reach more people.

The stricter reading also holds. At concentration index 1.22 the class is only marginally more outlier-weighted than the corpus baseline, nothing like `xpc-sync-wait` at 1.74 / 8 users, which is the shape of a genuinely single-machine class. It is also not the *most* widespread thing: `runloop-idle` (0.43) and `appkit` (0.58) are far more evenly spread, and `runloop-idle` was already ruled a non-hang in #411.

Severity says these are visible, not marginal. `generic-metadata` median stall **4566 ms**, p90 25.3 s, max 96.7 s, **49.3% at or above 5 s**. That is the second-highest median of any cause (behind `xpc-sync-wait` at 18.2 s) and above `swiftui-update` (3128 ms). A four to five second freeze is a beachball the operator sees.

Matched needles, so the bucket is not one rule doing all the work: `MetadataCacheKey` 302 hits, `swift_getTypeByMangledName` 202, `_swift_getGenericMetadata` 177, `instantiateGenericMetadata` 122, `swift_getOpaqueTypeMetadata` 72, `_gatherGenericParameters` 30. Leaf symbols are dominated by `MetadataCacheKey::operator==`, `getCache(TargetTypeContextDescriptor)` and `ConcurrentReadableHashMap::find<MetadataCacheKey>`: runtime generic-metadata cache lookup, not one pathological call site.

It spans releases (0.52.0 through 0.61.0) and is current: **54 events from 7 users on 0.61.0**, the latest public release, up to 2026-08-10.

### Half (b): blocked, and it will stay blocked until the classifier ships

The post-classifier per-cause Sentry trend **does not exist yet, and no verdict can be drawn from what is there.** Verified, not assumed:

- The classifier (#402, `5920e3bb0`) is in **no version tag**. `git tag --contains 5920e3bb0` returns only `xcframework-7604624d89...`. #411 (`b2fb5caa5`) is in no tag at all.
- Latest public GitHub release is **v0.61.0 (2026-07-29)**. Real users in the corpus are on 0.58.0 (3356 events) and 0.61.0 (1059).
- The only `main-thread-hang/*` issues in Sentry are three, carrying **7 events total, all from one user** (0D9CEF42, a maintainer machine, which is U11 in the corpus above): `runloop-idle` 3, `other` 3, `swiftui-update/hosting-begin-transaction` 1. Every one is a `staging.rel.v0.63.0` or `debug.*` build.
- There is **no `main-thread-hang/generic-metadata` issue in Sentry at all**. Zero events, because zero users run the classifier.

Anyone producing a "distinct-user volume" verdict from those 7 events is reading their own laptop.

### Observation window and minimum event count for the eventual verdict

The C11-192 review's S7 worry, that post-#401 throttling starves the trend, is **not supported by the data**. Reprojecting the corpus into the post-#401 shape (episodes only, recaptures dropped) still leaves `generic-metadata` at **65 episodes/week from 11 users**. Even a further order-of-magnitude fall in the fleet's hang rate leaves a readable signal.

Proposed pre-registration for when 0.63.0 (or its successor carrying #402 and #411) reaches the public channel:

- **Observation window: 14 days** of public release uptake, starting when the release has at least 10 distinct users reporting any Sentry event.
- **Minimum for a verdict: 25 `main-thread-hang/generic-metadata` events.** Below that, extend the window rather than call it.
- **Real class (open a fix ticket with a Time Profiler acceptance):** 5 or more distinct users, or a distinct-user count at or above 40% of the users appearing in any hang issue in the same window.
- **Not a real class (close with the evidence):** 2 or fewer distinct users after the full window at or above the minimum event count.
- Carry the median stall alongside. Under about 2 s the class stops being user-facing regardless of user spread.

### Recommendation, not yet acted on

I have **not** opened a fix ticket and have **not** closed this one. The (a) evidence is strong enough on its own to justify a fix ticket now (13 of 20 users, 4.6 s median, current on 0.61.0) without waiting on (b), but that is the operator's call and the ticket's stated close condition is the post-classifier trend, which is unobtainable today.

Script and raw output: `fetch_events.py`, `classify.py`, `episodes.py`, `classified.jsonl`, `classify_output.txt`, `episodes_output.txt` in the run scratchpad.

Fix ticket opened: C11-205, carrying the (a) evidence and a Time Profiler acceptance. The per-user spread was decisive enough on its own (13 of 20 users, 4,566 ms median, still live on 0.61.0) that waiting on the post-classifier trend to authorize a fix would have been the wrong trade.

This ticket keeps the (b) half: the post-classifier trend verdict, blocked until a public release carries #402. The pre-registered verdict criteria in the analysis comment above stand. Operator has queued a release pass (2026-08-10).
